elements.element: Audit frequency limited to no more than once per 12 months
elements.evidence: "conducted not more than once in any 12 month period"

elements.element: Auditing party (Vendor) bears cost of audit
elements.evidence: "The Party or Parties requesting the review or audit shall bear its costs"

elements.element: Cost-shift exception only where underpayment exceeds 5%
elements.evidence: "unless the review or audit reveals an underpayment exceeding 5%"

elements.element: No direct access to Customer systems
elements.evidence: "shall not include direct access to the audited Party's systems"

elements.element: Fallback: once per year audit frequency
elements.evidence: "not more than once in any 12 month period"
30 days' notice exceeds the 15-day fallback minimum

elements.element: Fallback: Vendor bears cost unless underpayment exceeds 10%
elements.evidence: "requesting the review or audit shall bear its costs unless ... underpayment exceeding 5%" (requesting party bears cost; threshold tighter than fallback)

reasons: All atomic elements of the locked preferred level are expressly present in the inserted paragraph 9.10: once per 12 months, 30 days' prior written notice, normal business hours, independent auditor bound by confidentiality, no direct system access, and requesting-party cost bearing with a 5% underpayment cost-shift trigger.
A concise single-paragraph insertion is appropriate because the original Paragraph 9 audit right was wholly unqualified; no untouched sentence was rewritten and the mutual drafting is preserved.

Minimality is short of clean: "and off-site where possible" adds a location restriction not required by the preferred position and introduces a soft, undefined qualifier ("where possible") that could be argued over; it should be deleted.

Minor residual tension worth noting rather than redlining: existing 9.8 lets the audited Party recover "the entire costs" from the requester unconditionally, and 9.8's third sentence allocates F&ASC-initiated audit costs per Schedule B, so the new 5% cost-shift exception overlays those mechanics; intent is nonetheless preserved and the overlay favours us.
